what: Suzano is the world's largest producer of hardwood pulp, grown from eucalyptus plantations in Brazil and shipped to paper mills worldwide. It also makes its own paper and tissue.
customers: Paper and tissue manufacturers in China, Europe and North America, plus Brazilian paper buyers.
money: printing paper, tissue and paperboard sold mostly in Brazil
moat: Brazilian eucalyptus grows in seven years rather than the decades softwood takes in the north, which makes Suzano the lowest-cost pulp producer on earth by a wide margin.
risks: Pulp is a commodity and the price swings hard with Chinese demand
$17.3B of debt, large even against $8.9B of revenue, much of it from the Cerrado mill
Most debt is in dollars while costs are in reais, so the exchange rate matters a great deal
opportunities: 7.2 times earnings with a 26.8% net margin and $977M of free cash flow
The new Cerrado mill is the largest single pulp line in the world and the cheapest to run
Analysts see about 30% upside, with 6 covering the stock
watch: Pulp prices in China and the pace of debt reduction after the Cerrado spending.
